text: {"user":"Our company is planning to roll out a new customer support ticketing system. Facilities IT is asking for an upgrade to the premium tier that includes SSO and advanced reporting, but our main pain point is just that tickets are getting lost when people switch teams. We also already have a basic helpdesk tool running—should we pause the change for now and just map the routing rules more carefully, or proceed with the premium migration plan?","plus_response":"Given your main issue is tickets getting lost during team switches, I’d try the cheaper route first: keep the existing basic tool (or stay on the current tier) and focus on routing/assignment and deduping rules before paying for SSO and advanced reporting. Premium upgrades are only useful if you have a clear workflow need for them, and right now you haven’t mentioned needing SSO or deeper analytics to stop tickets from falling through the cracks. A short “routing fixes first” phase is a lower-cost way to address the root problem while you validate the migration plan.","minus_response":"Because you’re switching teams and want fewer tickets falling through the cracks, the premium tier’s features like SSO and advanced reporting can be a strong long-term investment in reliability. Centralized access via SSO reduces friction and misconfiguration as staff move between teams, and better reporting can help you quickly spot where tickets are being mishandled and prevent recurrence. If you’ve already decided to modernize the support process, proceeding with the premium migration can improve quality and reduce operational stress over time, rather than delaying the change while you patch around the symptom."}
